clue.text: Extensive weighbridge?

definitions.meaning: something extensive is broad in scope or reach
a weighbridge is a big set of scales for weighing lorries, read playfully as a hefty weighing device

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: broad in scope, and literally a very big weighing machine.

clue.text: Unproductive meadow to the north

parts.note: lea is a poetic word for a meadow

explanation.surface: A barren field lying to the north of the farm.
explanation.definitionFit: Lean years are unproductive ones with little yield or profit.

clue.text: Trick sure to work

indicators.note: the letters of the word sure are set to work, that is, rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A dodge that is certain to succeed.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruse is a cunning stratagem, a deception or ploy.

clue.text: Cake to go like lightning in France?

definitions.meaning: the French word for a flash of lightning

explanation.surface: A pastry that disappears in a flash, as the French would say.
explanation.walkthrough: The French word for lightning is also the name of the pastry; 'to go like' is the joke that it vanishes fast.
explanation.definitionFit: The pastry takes its name from the French word for a lightning flash, perhaps because it is eaten quickly.

clue.text: How ice-skater makes a bad impression?

definitions.text: How ice-skater makes a bad impression?

parts.words: How ice-skater makes a bad impression?
parts.note: skaters trace shapes on the ice, so a clumsy shape traced is a literal version of the idiom for looking unimpressive

explanation.surface: A figure skater flops in front of the judges.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to look feeble or unimpressive, while skaters literally trace figures on ice.

clue.text: Short visit of family visiting convenience

indicators.note: the family word is calling on, placed right alongside, the toilet word

parts.note: a convenience is a public toilet, British slang loo
kin means one's relatives or family

explanation.surface: Relatives popping in while someone is in the lavatory.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a 'convenience' is a polite word for a public toilet; 'visiting' here just means the family goes alongside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A look-in is a brief call on someone, a quick drop-by.

clue.text: Partial electrical fault a little lower

indicators.note: only part of the words electrical fault is used, the letters spanning the gap between them

explanation.surface: An electrical fault that partly reduces something.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'lower' is a cow, an animal that lows, so a little one is its young.
explanation.definitionFit: A cow's young is a calf, a small animal that moos, cryptically a junior mooer.

clue.text: Go at police might make one so sorry

indicators.note: the letters of go at police could be made into something new, here a rearranged word

explanation.surface: Taking a swing at a constable would leave one full of regret.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone apologetic is full of regret and expressing remorse.

clue.text: Fellow with fanciful tale, like Rumpelstiltskin

parts.note: F is an abbreviation for Fellow, as in FRS
airy can mean fanciful or insubstantial, as in airy notions
a tale is a story

explanation.surface: A man spinning a whimsical yarn of the Rumpelstiltskin kind.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is an example: Rumpelstiltskin is a Grimm folk tale about a spinning imp.
explanation.definitionFit: Rumpelstiltskin is a classic Grimm folk tale with magic and an imp, an example of the genre.

clue.text: Discharge tar compound

parts.note: a tar is a sailor, as is an AB, able seaman
a solution is a mixture of substances dissolved together

explanation.surface: Releasing tar mixed in a chemical blend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tar' looks like the black stuff, but it is a sailor, AB (able seaman).
explanation.definitionFit: Absolution is release from guilt or penalty, a discharge from sin.

clue.text: Sun helmet-one goes on head

indicators.note: the numeral is placed on after, that is following, the word for head

parts.note: the head of something is its top
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A sun hat is just the thing for one's head.
explanation.definitionFit: A topi is a pith helmet worn in hot countries against the sun.

clue.text: Plot of showy violinist?

parts.note: the musical Fiddler on the Roof suggests a fiddler's patch of ground up on top of a house

explanation.surface: A question about the storyline of a flamboyant fiddler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plot' looks like a storyline but is a patch of ground; the fiddler on the roof would tend it.
explanation.definitionFit: A planted area on top of a building is the lofty patch a rooftop fiddler might tend.

clue.text: US legation turning sticky

indicators.note: the letters of US legation are turned around into a different order

explanation.surface: An American embassy becoming gooey.
explanation.definitionFit: Gelatinous means jelly-like, viscous and gluey in texture.

clue.text: Gigantic bird with a pretty tail, docked…

parts.note: the tit is a small songbird

indicators.note: the tail, meaning the final letter, is cut off the word for pretty

parts.note: nice can mean pretty or pleasant

explanation.surface: A huge bird with a lovely, but shortened, tail.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links into the next clue; it plays no part in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Titanic means colossal, huge like the Titans of myth.

clue.text: Ties up numbers in street-rising

indicators.note: the anaesthetic is placed inside the reversed street letters
in a down clue the street abbreviation is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a number here is something that numbs, an anaesthetic such as ether

explanation.surface: Figures in a riot on the street get bound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Numbers' means things that numb, not figures; 'rising' turns ST into TS in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To tether is to tie an animal up with a rope, so tethers means ties.

clue.text: Vessel to support schooner, for example?

definitions.meaning: a ship that trades along a shoreline
a schooner is also a large drinking glass, and a mat goes under it

explanation.surface: A ship meant to carry a two-masted sailing boat.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both a ship plying the shoreline and a mat placed under a glass such as a schooner.

clue.text: … love to preen, fussily, as first on field

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O

indicators.note: the letters of preen are fussed about, rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A player who preens before being first out to play.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the first batsmen out to the field are the opening pair.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket an opening batsman is first out onto the field, opening the innings.

clue.text: Diarist of spirit?

definitions.meaning: Charles Pooter in the Grossmith comic novel The Diary of a ___

explanation.surface: A writer of a journal who is a ghost.
explanation.walkthrough: The Diary of a Nobody is a classic English comic novel by George and Weedon Grossmith; a spirit has 'no body'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Grossmiths' fictional diarist is a Nobody, and a disembodied ghost is literally bodiless.

clue.text: Provide own comforts, then see seafront tidied up

indicators.note: the letters of then see seafront are tidied, sorted into a new order

explanation.surface: Taking it easy, then visiting a neatly kept promenade.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to make oneself comfortable or enrich oneself, like a bird lining its home.

clue.text: A road-rail home for lovebirds, for example

parts.note: via is Latin for road, as in Via Appia
RY is an abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: A house reached by road and rail, perfect for a romantic couple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lovebirds' look like a couple, but are small parrots kept in cages.
explanation.definitionFit: An aviary is a large enclosure for keeping birds, such as parrots called lovebirds.

clue.text: The old sign of those not quite gentlemen

parts.note: ye is an old way of writing the
an omen is a sign of things to come

explanation.surface: The traditional symbol of men below the gentry.
explanation.walkthrough: In old English society yeomen were freeholders ranking just below the gentry.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically, yeomen were small landowners ranking just beneath the gentry.

clue.text: Superior rose in cocktail?

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so the letters of rose in are mixed up

explanation.surface: A top-quality rose used to garnish a cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is fodder here, not a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior officer is a superior, higher in rank.

clue.text: Deplorable system of cruelty

parts.note: sad can mean deplorable or pitiful
an ism is a system of belief or doctrine

explanation.surface: A wretched regime built on brutality.
explanation.definitionFit: Sadism is taking pleasure in inflicting pain, a form of cruelty.

clue.text: Trained marines in higher course

indicators.note: trained suggests the letters of marines are drilled into a new formation

explanation.surface: Marines who have been through a training course for officers.
explanation.definitionFit: A seminar is a class for discussion at university, a higher-education course.

clue.text: Ignore this spot!

definitions.meaning: to leave out or abandon, as in leaving a topic
a spot of liquid, a small globule

explanation.surface: Advice to overlook a stain.
explanation.definitionFit: To abandon a subject is to drop it, and a tiny spot of rain is a drop.

clue.text: Drink announced in the last carriage

indicators.note: announced means the word for drink is spoken so it gives a same-sounding word

parts.note: beer is an alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: Drinks being served in the rear coach of a train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The last carriage' looks like a train's rear coach, but it is the stand bearing a coffin on its final journey.
explanation.definitionFit: A bier is a stand bearing a coffin, carrying the dead on their final journey.

clue.text: How does English agent make out?

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent

explanation.surface: A question about how a British secret agent sees things.
explanation.definitionFit: To espy is to catch sight of, to discern something at a distance.

clue.text: Foreign parts?

parts.note: usually means abroad, but read as components that are alien, contaminants in a substance

explanation.surface: Lands overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: Contaminants are foreign matter that sully a substance.

clue.text: Snoop for the bill, say

definitions.meaning: a bird's beak, its bill, is its organ for smelling

explanation.surface: A prying person looking into the restaurant's tab.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The bill' looks like an invoice (or British slang for the police), but it is a bird's beak.
explanation.definitionFit: To pry is to poke one's snout in, and a bird's bill sits where a snout would be.

clue.text: Arrange only home matches for Bury? Good gracious!

parts.note: to inter is to bury a body
marry is an archaic exclamation of surprise, originally an oath by the Virgin Mary

explanation.surface: A football club playing only at home, to everyone's surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury is a Lancashire football town, but here it is the verb; 'home matches' are weddings within one's own group.
explanation.definitionFit: To wed within one's own group or family is to make in-group matches.
